subject: Proposal: Willful misconduct / fraud thresholds for MSA amendment
messages:
From: Marcus R. Hale <marcus.hale@bluewave.io>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
Cc: BlueWave Legal <contracts@bluewave.io>, BlueWave Procurement <procurement@bluewave.io>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — willful misconduct / fraud carve-out

Tessa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround last week. Attached are our clean redlines for the MSA (BlueWave_MSARedlines_v3.docx). Two items we want to call out before we dig into line edits:

1) The willful misconduct / fraud exception — our GC asks that fraud be an absolute carve-out (no cap, no liability cap applies) and that the threshold be ‘intentional or knowing fraudulent conduct’.
2) The proposed materiality threshold for gross negligence — we prefer ‘material breach caused by reckless or grossly negligent acts’ and want a bright-line: $250k or 6 months’ fees, whichever is greater.

Those two points are likely to be deal-breakers for us if we can’t get to mutually acceptable language quickly. Can Redwood provide a counter that preserves the integrity of the exception while giving us a predictable cap?

—Marcus
Director, Strategic Sourcing
BlueWave, Inc.

Attachments: BlueWave_MSARedlines_v3.docx (docx)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
To: Marcus R. Hale <marcus.hale@bluewave.io>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — willful misconduct / fraud carve-out

Marcus — thanks for the note and the redlines. We took a quick pass with legal and procurement and want to propose a compromise that addresses predictability for both sides. High level: Redwood cannot agree to a blanket no-cap for fraud (open-ended exposure) but we are willing to accept an exception for proven fraud/willful misconduct subject to a higher, well-defined threshold tied to demonstrable loss and a fraud-finding standard.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Fraud / willful misconduct: Exception from monetary cap only where there is a final judicial or arbitration determination of fraud or intentional misconduct.
- Threshold for uncapped relief: demonstrated direct damages exceeding $500,000 OR cumulative Redwood billings to BlueWave under the Order Form exceeding $1,000,000.
- For reckless or gross negligence: keep within the overall cap but remove limitations for consequential damages where the reckless act is a proximate cause of third-party liability (limited carve-out language).

We attached a short counterproposal (Redwood_counterproposal_0809.pdf) with redline snippets. Neha — can you confirm we are comfortable with the judicial/arbitral final determination language and the numeric thresholds? Lauren — we may need your help drafting fallback wording that ties the uncapped carve-out to a ‘final determination’ clause and defines acceptable evidentiary standards.

Next step: Marcus, if this framing looks workable I’ll ask legal to send formal redline language by EOD tomorrow. If not, let us know the priority items so we can escalate.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — willful misconduct / fraud carve-out

Tessa / Dev —

Spoke with Lauren this morning. A few legal points and suggested wording to preserve Redwood’s exposure profile while giving BlueWave the remedial certainty they want:

1) Final determination: we can accept ‘final judicial or arbitral determination’ but we should add a provision that allows an interim enforcement mechanism where preliminary injunctions or criminal indictments accompanied by seizure orders will allow limited provisional relief pending final determination (this helps with fraud that involves obvious diversion of funds).

2) Thresholds: instead of a single-dollar bright line we recommend a two-factor threshold: (a) demonstrated direct monetary loss >= $500,000 and (b) Redwood billings to BlueWave in the prior 12 months >= $750,000. Both must be met to trigger uncapped relief. Rationale: protects Redwood from unlimited exposure on small deals while giving BlueWave protection on enterprise-scale impact.

3) Reckless/gross negligence: keep within cap but we will accept an exception to exclusion for consequential damages where Redwood’s reckless act is the proximate cause of third-party liability — limited to direct third-party defense costs with a sub-cap (we suggest $1,000,000).

4) Evidence standard: ‘clear and convincing evidence’ for fraud/willful misconduct findings before uncapped liability applies.

I’m attaching a two-paragraph redline snippet (pasted below) that Lauren has preliminarily signed off on. If this looks ok to you, we should route to procurement for quick acceptance or flag items they will push back on.

--- pasted redline snippet ---
Willful misconduct / fraud: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the parties acknowledge that proven fraud or intentional misconduct by a party shall not be subject to the monetary limitations of liability set forth herein, provided that (i) there is a final judicial or arbitral determination of such fraud or intentional misconduct, or (ii) where a governmental criminal indictment or a court-ordered seizure of assets has been entered and such action remains in effect following a 30-day cure period. Notwithstanding the foregoing, uncapped liability under this section shall only be available where (A) the claimant demonstrates direct monetary loss of at least $500,000 and (B) Redwood’s aggregate billings to Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim exceed $750,000. The standard of proof for triggering uncapped liability shall be clear and convincing evidence.
--- end snippet ---

Comments welcome. If procurement pushes hard on a single-dollar lower number, we can consider replacing the aggregate-billing gate with ‘six months’ fees’ tied to the Order Form, but that introduces circularity and potential gaming here.

Neha
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_counterproposal_0809.pdf

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — willful misconduct / fraud carve-out

Agree with Neha — the two-factor gate plus clear-and-convincing standard is the right commercial compromise. A couple of practical points before we send final redlines to BlueWave:

- We should replace any absolute grand-fathering language in their Order Form references with a defined ‘Order Form Revenue’ clause so both sides can compute the billing trigger deterministically. I can draft that short definitional clause.
- For the provisional relief language, limit Redwood’s interim exposure to escrowed funds or retention of disputed amounts only where there is a court order — we don’t want procurement executing chargebacks on a presumption of fraud.

If Tessa approves, I’ll produce the formal redline and send to Marcus and CC Dev for a technical note on how we collect and provide billing evidence (billing CSV + HubSpot invoice trail).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
